name: deja-vu
tagline: A memory layer for coding agents that indexes existing logs
description: deja-vu is a memory layer for coding agents that indexes the logs already on disk — from Claude Code, Codex, and opencode — so past sessions become retrievable context. It reports an 84.9 percent hit@1 retrieval rate with 7-9ms searches, and it does all of this without any LLM calls or embeddings. Instead of building a separate memory store that agents must be trained to use, deja-vu treats the logs agents already produce as the source of truth. It is written in Go and engineered to be fast and local-first.
highlights: Indexes existing agent logs (Claude Code, Codex, opencode) as retrievable memory
No LLM calls and no embeddings required
Local-first memory that uses the logs agents already produce
curatorNote: The cleverest part is not building a new memory store but indexing the logs agents already write. Near-instant search with no LLM or embeddings makes it a genuinely cheap way to give agents persistence.
